title: The Forty-Fourth Floor to the Rayburn Building: Leon Black, Apollo, and the Fee
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Manhattan, the birth
stops.date_confidence: The date, 31 July 1951, is attested in the Wikipedia infobox and independently corroborated by Black's own letter of 25 January 2021, which speaks of nearing his seventieth birthday that July. The birthplace is not attested: the article's birth_place field is empty and no source reached in this pass names a city, hospital, or neighbourhood. New York is an inference from the family's residence and the pin is a general Manhattan point.
stops.campa: Leon David Black is born on the last day of July to Eli Black and Shirley Lubell Black. His father was born Elihu Menashe Blachowicz in Lublin in 1921, came to America a rabbi's son, trained as a rabbi himself, and left the pulpit for balance sheets. The house the boy grows up in is a house of acquisition: banana boats, refrigerated holds, a Central American revenue stream, a conglomerate built up around the old United Fruit Company. The name on the letterhead is United Brands. The boats and the plantations are the ones United Fruit already owned.
suggested_refs: The United Brands Company annual reports of the early 1970s, successor filings to United Fruit

stops.name: Hanover, philosophy and history
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 1973. Wikipedia gives the degree as an AB in philosophy and history and does not say summa cum laude; that honour comes from Dartmouth's own trustee biography of Black and is carried here on that source alone, re-attributed away from Wikipedia. Month and day of commencement are not documented and default to June; the pin is the main quadrangle.
stops.campa: Four years in Hanover, and in 1973 an AB in philosophy and history. The college's own trustee biography adds summa cum laude to the line; the standard reference does not carry it. He reads in a New Hampshire valley three hundred miles north of Park Avenue and the banana trade, an undergraduate with a good transcript and a father who runs a conglomerate. In thirty-nine years his name will be cut into the front of a building on this campus. The petitions to take it down come nine years after that.
suggested_refs: The Dartmouth trustee biography of Leon Black, which alone carries the summa cum laude

stops.name: Cambridge, the business school
stops.date_confidence: The MBA is attested to 1975. The month of matriculation is not documented and defaults to September; the pin is Baker Library on the Allston campus.
stops.campa: He crosses the river to Allston and enters the business school, two years of case studies and cold calls in the Baker Library reading room. He is twenty-two when he arrives. In February of his second year his father goes out of a sealed window on Park Avenue, and Black sits his examinations in the weeks while the whole financial press works out why. What the surname means to everyone in the room has changed by the spring. The MBA is conferred on schedule in 1975.
suggested_refs: Harvard Business School class of 1975 records

stops.name: Pan Am Building, the forty-fourth floor
stops.date_confidence: The date, the building, and the floor are attested. Two errors in the working dossier are corrected rather than smoothed over. First, the Securities and Exchange Commission's disclosure came weeks after the death, and its suit was filed in April 1975, roughly two months later, not days before it. Second, of the bribe agreed with Honduran president Oswaldo Lopez Arellano, commonly reported at $2.5 million, the sum actually authorised and paid was $1.25 million.
stops.campa: On a Monday morning Eli Black takes his attache case, breaks the sealed window of his office on the forty-fourth floor, and steps out over the northbound Park Avenue viaduct. He is fifty-three. He leaves no note. His son is at business school in Massachusetts. Weeks later the Securities and Exchange Commission tells the public what the dead man had been carrying: United Brands paid the president of Honduras to cut the banana export tax. Of the two and a half million agreed, one and a quarter million was authorised and paid, and it moved through Switzerland.
sources: SEC v. United Brands Company, filed April 1975
U.S. State Department memorandum on the United Brands and Honduras affair, history.state.gov
suggested_refs: The Pan Am Building, now the MetLife Building, 200 Park Avenue

stops.name: Midtown, the accountant
stops.date_confidence: The Peat Marwick and Boardroom Reports employment is attested by Wikipedia on the authority of a named Bloomberg Businessweek profile of January 2020, which is ordinary biographical sourcing; the working pool's caution flag on it is not carried. Exact dates and office addresses are undocumented and the pin is a general Midtown point. The Lehman anecdote in the same campa is tradition: it recurs in profiles of Black, no interview record has ever been produced, and it is marked here as legend rather than fact.
stops.campa: The son of a dead conglomerate chairman goes to work as an accountant at Peat Marwick, and then for the business publisher Boardroom Reports, footing columns and checking other men's arithmetic. Every profile written since tells the same story about these years: Lehman Brothers turned him away for wanting the brains and the personality for Wall Street. Nobody has produced the interview or the interviewer. It is the reversal the whole later career gets narrated against. Who said it, and in what year, no profile has ever managed to say.
sources: Caleb Melby and Heather Perlberg, 'Nobody Makes Money Like Apollo's Ruthless Founder Leon Black,' Bloomberg Businessweek, 16 January 2020
suggested_refs: The Bloomberg Businessweek profile of January 2020, the earliest reachable carrier of the Lehman anecdote

stops.name: 60 Broad Street, the high-yield desk
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 1977; month and day are not documented and default to January. The pin is Drexel Burnham Lambert's New York headquarters at 60 Broad Street. Michael Milken's high-yield operation itself ran out of Beverly Hills, and no source reached places Black there rather than in New York.
stops.campa: Drexel Burnham Lambert hires him in 1977 and he moves up through it: managing director, head of mergers and acquisitions, co-head of corporate finance. The engine of the firm is Michael Milken's high-yield desk, which lends to companies the ratings agencies will not touch and finances raiders against companies that thought themselves safe. Black is the man who structures the takeovers the bonds pay for. The annual bondholders' conference takes its name from Connie Bruck's book about it: the Predators' Ball.
sources: James B. Stewart, Den of Thieves (1991)
suggested_refs: Drexel Burnham Lambert headquarters, 60 Broad Street, New York

stops.name: 60 Broad Street, six felonies
stops.date_confidence: Attested to December 1988; the day is not in the pool and defaults to the first. The working dossier described this as a plea of no contest in 1990, which is wrong twice over and is corrected rather than resolved silently: Drexel entered an Alford plea, a guilty plea entered while maintaining innocence, to six felony counts, three of stock parking and three of stock manipulation, and paid a $650 million fine. The bankruptcy is a separate event fourteen months later and has its own stop.
stops.campa: The firm pleads to six felonies, three counts of parking stock and three of manipulating it, and pays six hundred and fifty million dollars. The plea is an Alford plea: guilty in law, innocent in the defendant's own mouth. Milken is indicted separately three months later and will go to prison. What Black has learned by 1988 is not how to price a bond but how a capital structure comes apart. He is not charged with anything, then or afterwards. He stays.
sources: James B. Stewart, Den of Thieves (1991)
suggested_refs: The December 1988 plea agreement between Drexel Burnham Lambert and the United States

stops.name: 60 Broad Street, Chapter Eleven
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Drexel Burnham Lambert filed for Chapter 11 on 13 February 1990.
stops.campa: Fourteen months after the plea the firm files for bankruptcy and stops existing. The junk-bond inventory it underwrote is scattered across savings and loans and insurance companies that regulators are now forcing to sell, at whatever price a buyer will name. Black is thirty-eight, out of work, and carrying in his head the map of who owns which distressed piece of paper and how badly they need to be rid of it. Within about six months he has raised four hundred million dollars against that map.
suggested_refs: The Drexel Burnham Lambert Chapter 11 petition, 13 February 1990

segments.name: Apollo Raised Out of the Wreck

stops.name: 9 West 57th Street, the first fund
stops.date_confidence: The founding is attested to 1990; the month is not documented and defaults to June, consistent with the reported six-month interval after Drexel's February collapse. The 1990 office address is recorded nowhere reached in this pass. The pin is 9 West 57th Street, the Solow Building, confirmed as Apollo's headquarters on the letterhead of Black's own investor letter of 25 January 2021; the pool's coordinate for this stop was byte-identical with the MoMA pin and is not used.
stops.campa: Apollo Advisors is founded by Black with Joshua Harris, Marc Rowan, and Antony Ressler, all of them out of the wreck of Drexel, and the first fund closes at roughly four hundred million dollars. The thesis is the one the collapse handed them: buy distressed debt from sellers who are being made to sell, take the equity when the company reorganises, hold it until somebody wants it again. Nobody else wants the paper at the price the forced sellers will take.
sources: SEC EDGAR, Apollo Global Management corporate filings and prospectuses
suggested_refs: The Solow Building, 9 West 57th Street, Apollo's long-standing headquarters

stops.name: Los Angeles, the Executive Life portfolio
stops.date_confidence: November 1991 is attested for the sale of the portfolio; the day is not documented and defaults to the first. The pin is a Los Angeles city-centre placeholder, no office address having been verified. The dossier's framing is corrected: the purchaser of record was Altus Finance, a unit of Credit Lyonnais, for $3.25 billion, and Credit Lyonnais was later shown to be the real buyer through secret agreements. Apollo and Lion Advisors managed the portfolio and shared in its gains; California's later expanded complaint reached Apollo-affiliated parties. No criminal conviction attaches to Black in this matter.
stops.campa: Executive Life Insurance Company is seized by California regulators, insolvent on a junk-bond portfolio underwritten largely by Drexel. The bonds go to Altus Finance, a Credit Lyonnais unit, at a distressed valuation; Apollo and Lion Advisors manage them and take a share of what comes back. The bonds recover. Annuitants who never chose the risk take the losses, and the litigation runs through the courts for two decades. California's attorney general eventually alleges the whole thing was a scheme and names Apollo entities in it.
sources: California Attorney General press release, 'Lockyer Expands Lawsuit Alleging Conspiracy to Raid Executive Life,' oag.ca.gov
suggested_refs: The California Insurance Department's 1999 action against Credit Lyonnais and Altus Finance

stops.name: Washington, the Melanoma Research Alliance
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 2007 by the organisation's own account. Month and day are not given and default to January; the pin is the alliance's Washington headquarters at 730 15th Street NW, not the place of the founding decision.
stops.campa: Debra Black is diagnosed with melanoma. She survives it, and the couple commit twenty-five million dollars to found the Melanoma Research Alliance under the auspices of the Milken Institute, aimed at a cancer that then had almost no research money behind it. This is the philanthropy with nothing else attached to it. The alliance takes offices on Fifteenth Street in Washington and becomes the largest private funder of melanoma work in the country.
sources: curemelanoma.org, 'From Health Scare to Transformative Change'
suggested_refs: The Melanoma Research Alliance, founded 2007 under the auspices of the Milken Institute

stops.name: Midtown, Elysium Management
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 2008 by the Dechert LLP memorandum; month and day are not given and default to January. The street address of Elysium Management is not documented in anything reached in this pass and the pin is a general Midtown point.
stops.campa: He sets up a family office and calls it Elysium, the field where the favoured dead go. It is his own money, staffed and lawyered apart from Apollo. It holds the investments, the trusts, the property, the aircraft, the pictures, and the estate plan. It is also the entity that will sign a services agreement with Jeffrey Epstein, receive his tax opinions, wire his fees, and lend to his companies. It begins in 2008 with a single employee. By 2014 there are about ten.
sources: Dechert LLP memorandum to the Apollo Global Management conflicts committee, filed as Ex-99.1 to Apollo's Form 8-K, 25 January 2021
suggested_refs: Elysium Management LLC, the Black family office

stops.name: Wilmington, the Chancery and the billion
stops.date_confidence: The Settlement Agreement is dated 14 December 2008; Huntsman terminated the merger on 13 December. The deal size circulates two ways and both are recorded: $6.5 billion, the figure in the July 2007 merger agreement, and $10.6 billion, the enterprise value including assumed debt. The claim that Black personally agreed to contribute up to $60 million is rejected on the primary document: the Settlement Agreement, which he signs as a party, expressly excepts Leon Black and Joshua J. Harris from joint and several liability for sums due Huntsman, and no such figure appears in it or the side letter. The $60 million in the Black record belongs to a different transaction, Epstein's later fee demand. The coordinate is corrected to the Leonard L. Williams Justice Center, 500 N. King Street.
stops.campa: Apollo's chemicals company Hexion agrees to buy Huntsman, then tries to walk away when the credit market closes, arguing the target has become insolvent. The Court of Chancery finds Hexion knowingly breached its obligations. The settlement comes to a billion dollars: a three hundred and twenty-five million dollar termination fee, four hundred and twenty-five million in cash from the Apollo affiliates, and two hundred and fifty million of Huntsman convertible notes taken up. Black signs the agreement as a party. Paragraph three excepts him by name from paying anything under it.
sources: Hexion Specialty Chemicals Form 8-K filed 15 December 2008, accession 0000898822-08-001236, including the Settlement Agreement at Ex-10.1
Huntsman Corporation press release, 'Huntsman Terminates Merger Agreement and Settles With Hexion/Apollo'
suggested_refs: Hexion Specialty Chemicals v. Huntsman Corp., Delaware Court of Chancery, 2008

stops.name: 11 Wall Street, the opening bell
stops.date_confidence: The offering priced on 29 March 2011 at $19.00 a share and the final prospectus, Form 424B4, was filed 30 March; Wikipedia gives 29 March for the NYSE listing. The dossier's 5 April date belongs to a reported bell-ringing ceremony that could not be verified in this pass and is not used. Epstein's purchase of 263,257 shares is placed by the Dechert memorandum in March 2011, and the share count is exact in that primary document.
stops.campa: Apollo lists on the New York Stock Exchange at nineteen dollars a share and raises about five hundred and sixty-five million. Among the buyers in the offering is Financial Trust Company, of St. Thomas in the United States Virgin Islands, which takes two hundred sixty-three thousand two hundred fifty-seven shares. The order goes through the book like any other. Financial Trust is Jeffrey Epstein's. He has been a social friend of the chairman for fifteen years by now, and a director of his family foundation for fourteen.
sources: Apollo Global Management Form 424B4 prospectus, accession 0001193125-11-082478
suggested_refs: The Apollo Global Management initial public offering prospectus, March 2011

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the introduction
stops.date_confidence: The Dechert LLP memorandum, read here in the primary SEC exhibit, says only that Black was introduced to Epstein in the mid-1990s by a mutual friend and gives no year anywhere. The 1995 carried in the working dossier is invented precision; the date here is a placeholder to order the segment and should be read as mid-1990s. Dechert also does not say where the introduction took place. The pin is the canonical 9 East 71st Street coordinate shared with the Epstein and Maxwell files, the house Black is documented as visiting regularly, not the site of a first meeting.
stops.campa: A mutual friend introduces them. Jeffrey Epstein is living in the Herbert N. Straus mansion off Central Park, seven limestone storeys he did not buy, and he collects people the way other men collect pictures: physicists, presidents, financiers, anyone whose presence certifies the room. Black comes to the house regularly over the next two decades, to discuss business or to meet whoever else has been assembled that evening. For the first fifteen years nothing is billed and nothing is signed.
stops.quote: Friendship is an amorphous term. This is somebody who knew intimately the goings on in my family tax and estate planning entities.
stops.quote_source: Leon Black, House Oversight Committee transcribed interview, 26 June 2026, as reported by ABC News, 17 July 2026
sources: jeffrey_epstein.journey.json, '9 East 71st Street, the Straus house'
suggested_refs: The Herbert N. Straus House, 9 East 71st Street, Manhattan

stops.name: Midtown, a director of the family foundation
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 1997 by the Dechert memorandum as summarised in the working dossier; month and day are not given and default to January. No address is recorded for the Black Family Foundation in anything reached in this pass, and the pin is Black's own office at 9 West 57th Street.
stops.campa: Two years or so after the introduction, Epstein is made an initial director of the Black Family Foundation. He is a man with no charitable record of his own, handed a seat at the table where a billionaire's giving is decided. He resigns in 2007, and the foundation's Form 990 filings go on listing him through 2012, five years after he has gone. Which of the two records is the true one, the resignation or the filings, is a question nobody has answered on paper.
suggested_refs: The Black Family Foundation Form 990 series, which lists Epstein five years past his resignation

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the birthday album
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 2003 in the working dossier, citing the album later made public; the verification pass did not view the page itself. Month and day are not given and default to January. A bound album is an object rather than an event at an address, and the pin is the canonical townhouse coordinate.
stops.campa: For Epstein's fiftieth birthday Ghislaine Maxwell assembles a leather album of pages from his friends, letters and drawings and jokes, to be bound and handed over. In 2003 it is a birthday present among friends. Twenty years later the volume is read aloud in a federal courtroom and reproduced in the newspapers, by which time what it was celebrating has acquired a different name. The page Black sends in is a poem, written out in his own hand and bound in among the rest.
sources: leon_black.dossier.md, citing the birthday album as later publicly released
suggested_refs: The fiftieth-birthday album compiled for Jeffrey Epstein, 2003, later entered into the public record

stops.name: Palm Beach, the plea and after
stops.date_confidence: Epstein's Florida guilty plea is attested to June 2008; the day is not in the pool and defaults to the first. The Dechert memorandum does not name the El Brillo Way house: it says only that Black 'also briefly visited Epstein in Florida on one or two occasions.' The address is therefore an inference, flagged here, and the pin is the canonical 358 El Brillo Way coordinate already used in the Epstein file.
stops.campa: Epstein pleads guilty in Florida state court to soliciting prostitution and to procuring a person under eighteen for prostitution. Four years from now Black will put him on a retainer. He serves about thirteen months of an eighteen-month sentence, on work release for most of it, and is a registered sex offender from this point forward, publicly and searchably. Black visits him in Florida once or twice, by the Dechert review's account, and keeps the friendship going.
stops.quote: He enjoyed the company of good-looking women, and he was a bachelor.
stops.quote_source: Leon Black on Jeffrey Epstein, House Oversight Committee transcribed interview, 26 June 2026, as reported by ABC News, 17 July 2026
suggested_refs: The 2007 federal non-prosecution agreement and the June 2008 Florida state plea

stops.name: Little Saint James, twice with the family
stops.date_confidence: The Dechert memorandum records two visits with Black's family and states he never stayed overnight; no dates are given for either. The pool places them loosely in the 2010s and the date here is a placeholder to order the segment. The pin is the canonical Little Saint James coordinate shared with the Epstein and Maxwell files. Black says he did not know of Epstein's trafficking.
stops.campa: Seventy-odd acres of volcanic rock off St. Thomas: a colonnaded villa, guest cabanas, a helipad, and a striped temple on the point. Black goes twice, with his family, and by his own account never stays the night. Boat crews on St. Thomas have had their own name for the island for years by then. Whether a visitor arriving by tender for an afternoon would see anything of what the accusers describe is a question the Dechert lawyers put to him and answered in his favour, and that other people have gone on asking since.
sources: jeffrey_epstein.journey.json, 'Little Saint James, the island bought'
suggested_refs: Little Saint James, U.S. Virgin Islands, and the 2020 territorial civil complaint describing it

stops.name: London, Phaidon
stops.date_confidence: Attested to 2012 by Wikipedia and the working dossier; month and day are not documented and default to January. Phaidon's London premises are not pinned to a verified historical address here and the coordinate is a general London point.
stops.campa: He buys Phaidon Press, the art-book publisher, which has been printing monographs and survey volumes since it was founded in Vienna in 1923. A man who buys paintings at auction now owns the house that prints the books explaining what the paintings are worth looking at. His name appears nowhere on the spines. The catalogue keeps appearing under its own name and its own editors, and the design goes on being the thing people notice first about a Phaidon book.
suggested_refs: Phaidon Press, founded Vienna 1923, acquired 2012

stops.name: Hanover, forty-eight million
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Dartmouth announced the naming on 29 March 2012 and the building opened that September. The gift is attested at $48 million from Leon and Debra Black.
stops.campa: Forty-eight million dollars from Leon and Debra Black builds a visual arts centre on the campus where he read philosophy and history, and the college puts the family name across the front of it. The building opens that September with studios, a film theatre, and workshops for making things, the whole of it given over to students learning to produce objects. Nine years later students and faculty will circulate petitions asking Dartmouth to strike the name, and Dartmouth will decline. The name is still on the building.
sources: Dartmouth News, 'Dartmouth Names Visual Arts Center in Honor of Leon Black Family,' 29 March 2012
suggested_refs: The Black Family Visual Arts Center, Dartmouth College, opened September 2012

stops.name: Sotheby's York Avenue, The Scream
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 2 May 2012, $119,922,500 including buyer's premium, then the highest price paid for any work of art at auction. Bidding opened at $40 million and ran more than twelve minutes; the winning bid came by telephone. The coordinate is corrected and normalised: the research pool gave Sotheby's New York three different pins across two lenses, none of them right, and all are set here to 40.7663, -73.9535, the geocode for 1334 York Avenue.
stops.campa: Bidding opens at forty million and runs twelve minutes. Black takes Edvard Munch's 1895 pastel of The Scream by telephone at one hundred nineteen million nine hundred twenty-two thousand five hundred dollars, a record for anything sold at auction anywhere. The consignor is a Norwegian shipowner's son whose father knew Munch. That October Black lends the pastel to the Museum of Modern Art, where it hangs until April, and it is the only version of the four the public sees for years before it goes back into a private collection.
sources: Sotheby's Impressionist and Modern Art evening sale record, 2 May 2012
suggested_refs: Munch's 1895 pastel of The Scream, exhibited at the Museum of Modern Art October 2012 to April 2013

stops.name: Sotheby's New Bond Street, the Raphael
stops.date_confidence: Corrected. The working dossier and Wikipedia's Leon Black article date the purchase to June 2013; that is when Black was revealed as the anonymous buyer and when the export licence was deferred, not when the drawing sold. The auction was December 2012, the auxiliary cartoon for the Head of a Young Apostle consigned by Peregrine Cavendish, 12th Duke of Devonshire, and sold for GBP 29.7 million. The day is not documented and defaults to the first. The pool left this as an unresolved year conflict; it is resolvable and is resolved here, with both dates named.
stops.campa: A red-chalk study by Raphael for a head in the Transfiguration, drawn about 1519 and kept at Chatsworth for two centuries, comes up at Sotheby's on New Bond Street and goes for twenty-nine point seven million pounds to an anonymous telephone. Six months later the buyer is named and the British culture minister defers the export licence, holding the drawing in the country while a domestic institution is invited to match the price. No institution matches it.
sources: The Independent, 'New York billionaire Leon Black's bid to take GBP 29m Raphael from UK blocked by Ed Vaizey,' 20 June 2013
suggested_refs: Raphael, auxiliary cartoon for the Head of a Young Apostle, sold Sotheby's London December 2012

stops.name: Sotheby's York Avenue, the Bomberg Talmud
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 22 December 2015, $9.3 million, described by Sotheby's as a new world auction record for any piece of Judaica. Coordinate normalised to 1334 York Avenue as at the Scream stop.
stops.campa: Nine point three million dollars for a complete Babylonian Talmud printed by Daniel Bomberg in Venice in the 1520s, a Christian printer's edition whose page every subsequent Talmud in the world still copies. Sotheby's calls the price a world auction record for any piece of Judaica. Bomberg set the Mishnah in the middle and ran the commentaries around it, and the folio numbering he chose became the address system by which a Jewish argument cites itself. Fewer than a dozen complete sets are known.
suggested_refs: The Bomberg Babylonian Talmud, Venice 1519-1523, whose pagination all later editions follow

stops.name: Southampton, the addresses
stops.date_confidence: The Southampton beachfront compound on Meadow Lane is attested by Wikipedia; no parcel, price, or acquisition date is documented, and the coordinate is corrected to the Meadow Lane strip itself, the pool's point having fallen several kilometres inland. The date is taken from the one dated property event in the campa, the Faena House listing reported by Bloomberg on 3 May 2016. The Beverly Hills estate, roughly $38 million in 2016 and roughly $47 million on sale in March 2026, is from Wikipedia; the Belgravia townhouse at about GBP 21 million is press reporting only, unverified against any land record, and is marked as such.
stops.campa: A beachfront compound on Meadow Lane, the Southampton strip the local papers call Billionaire Lane, is the summer address; the primary house is in Manhattan. In Miami Beach there is a Faena House apartment, put on the market in 2016 with Oren Alexander as the listing agent. In Beverly Hills there is the estate that used to be Tom Cruise's, bought the same year for about thirty-eight million and sold ten years later for about forty-seven. In London a Belgravia townhouse is reported at some twenty-one million pounds, on nobody's land record that this pass could reach.
sources: Bloomberg, 'Leon Black Selling at Miami's New Billionaire Condo Tower,' 3 May 2016
suggested_refs: Meadow Lane, Southampton, New York; Faena House, 3315 Collins Avenue, Miami Beach

stops.name: 980 Madison Avenue, the Picasso
stops.date_confidence: The dispute over Picasso's plaster Bust of a Woman (Marie-Therese) is attested; trial was set for September 2016 and the matter settled by June 2016, Black keeping the sculpture and Maya Widmaier-Picasso paying Pelham an undisclosed sum. The day is not documented and defaults to the first. The coordinate is corrected to the geocode for 980 Madison Avenue; the settlement itself was not concluded at the gallery.
stops.campa: Two buyers claim the same plaster: Black, through the dealer Pelham, and the Qatari royal family, through Larry Gagosian, each holding that they bought Pablo Picasso's Bust of a Woman from the artist's daughter. She had sold it twice, or is said to have. The litigation runs across two continents and settles weeks before trial, with Black keeping the sculpture. Going through his art files four years later, the Dechert lawyers find Epstein's advice among the papers on the contested Picasso.
suggested_refs: Picasso, Bust of a Woman (Marie-Therese), 1931, and the 2016 Pelham-Gagosian settlement

stops.name: Midtown, the agreement of thirteen February
stops.date_confidence: Corrected from the pool, which gave 2012 as the year of the formal retainer. The Dechert memorandum, read here in the primary exhibit at pp.5 and 15, has Epstein beginning work on the 2006 grantor retained annuity trust problem in late 2012, with the written services agreement, between Black and Southern Trust Company, Inc., drafted by Black's counsel and signed on 13 February 2013. First payment $15 million on 15 February 2013; second $8.5 million on 15 October 2013. The pin is a general Midtown point for Elysium Management, whose street address is undocumented.
stops.campa: A grantor retained annuity trust set up in 2006 has gone wrong, and the error is expensive. Epstein, who holds no professional qualification of any kind in tax, works out a fix. Black's own counsel drafts a services agreement between him and Southern Trust Company, Epstein's Virgin Islands entity, and it is signed on the thirteenth of February. Nothing in it requires the adviser to hold a licence. Two days later fifteen million dollars is wired. In October another eight and a half million follows.
stops.quote: The rates Black paid Epstein were 30 times higher than he paid the elite tax and estate advisors he already employed.
stops.quote_source: Senate Finance Committee ranking member's release, 'Continuing Epstein Investigation: Wyden Questions Leon Black,' 23 March 2026
suggested_refs: The Black and Southern Trust Company services agreement, signed 13 February 2013

stops.name: Tempe, the Origins Project
stops.date_confidence: The Dechert memorandum records charitable transfers made at Epstein's request, among them a donation to Arizona State University's Origins Project. No date and no amount are given anywhere in the pool; the date here is a placeholder to order the segment and should be read only as 'during the paid years.'
stops.campa: Among the charitable transfers the Dechert review traces to Epstein's direction is a gift to the Origins Project at Arizona State, a cosmology and physics programme that ran conferences putting famous scientists in rooms with famous donors. Epstein cultivated academics for thirty years and paid for the rooms they met in. The review gives no date for this gift and no amount, so where it falls among the paid years is a guess. What Black gives here he gives because his adviser asked for it.
suggested_refs: The Origins Project, Arizona State University, and its donor conferences

stops.name: Midtown, the loans to Plan D
stops.date_confidence: Corrected from the pool, which dated these to January 2017. The Dechert memorandum at p.17 says only 'in early 2017' and gives no month; January here is a placeholder. Two loans, $22.5 million and $8 million, from Black's BV70 LLC to Epstein's Plan D LLC, in connection with an art transaction. Black demanded repayment in full in early 2018 and Epstein repaid only $10 million, which corrects the pool's placement of the repayment 'before his death' and leaves roughly $20.5 million outstanding, a figure Dechert elsewhere rounds to $20 million.
stops.campa: Thirty and a half million dollars goes out in two loans from one of Black's companies to one of Epstein's, in connection with an art transaction, secured by nothing the record names. A year later Black demands the whole of it back. Epstein returns ten million and stops there. It is the last money that moves in that direction. The balance, about twenty and a half million, is still outstanding when he is arrested, and the lender and the estate argue about it afterwards among all the other claims.
suggested_refs: BV70 LLC to Plan D LLC, the two 2017 loans and the 2018 demand

stops.name: Midtown, the last payment
